Competitor News.copy:
Brighton's Amex Stadium could host matches at the 2035 Women's World Cup, after a successful bid from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales. The ground was among 19 venues listed as possible host stadiums at a FIFA meeting yesterday after football’s governing body gave its approval to the plans.

The 104-match tournament will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the UK since 1966. Brighton and Hove City Council previously expressed a desire to become one of the host cities for the tournament in late 2025, highlighting potential benefits including tourism and global media exposure.

Wider Sports News.title: Kraft Heinz isn’t afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship
Wider Sports News.summary: Kraft Heinz isn’t afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship Marketing Brew
Wider Sports News.copy:
The NFL has gotten a little bit cheesier this season—and fans can’t just blame the league’s scriptwriters. Earlier this year, Kraft Heinz inked a five-year, global partnership with the league for brands in its portfolio including Kraft, Velveeta, Philadelphia, and Kraft Mac & Cheese. It’s the first time multiple Kraft Heinz brands have been involved in the same long-term partnership, according to Ryan Djabbarah, the company’s head of sports and entertainment marketing—and halfway through the season, his team is already seeing results.

Their strategy, Djabbarah told Marketing Brew, has been based largely on weaving Kraft Heinz brands into NFL fan experiences in ways that are whimsical and funny while also adding value—like their latest activation, which reimagines end-zone pylons as blocks of cheese for Thanksgiving weekend as part of a Velveeta product giveaway.

Sixty-nine years after England lifted the men’s trophy at Wembley, the UK is set to host the World Cup again. FIFA’s Congress meets today, Monday 23rd November, to ratify England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales as co-hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The four nations are the only bidders, and member associations will vote at a specially arranged virtual meeting while a UK delegation attends Fifa’s Zurich headquarters. Wider Sports News.summary: MLB’s Local Media Rights Emerge As Focus in Labor Fight Front Office Sports
Wider Sports News.copy:
The future of MLB’s local media business has become a central element in the sport’s labor battle, providing yet another substantial layer to the already fractious situation. For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. Most recently, management has updated its cap offer to the MLB Players Association to a 2028 implementation, and vows there will be “no compromise” on the pursuit of a cap as the Dec. 1 expiration of the current labor deal and an expected lockout thereafter approach.

The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans. Throughout the entrenched negotiations, though, two key questions have persisted: Why are the local media and salary cap issues so deeply linked, and why couldn’t owners just agree on their own to pool that revenue, similar to how the NFL operates?

Rugby.title: Dan Sheehan learns his fate after 'Croc Roll' hearing
Rugby.summary: The Ireland captain's international season is over after red card is upheld.
Rugby.copy:
Ireland’s stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two matches for the croc roll that earned him a red card against South Africa last weekend. Sheehan, who started at No.8 for the first time in his 42-cap Ireland career in the 20-17 win, was sin-binned for the act of foul play on South Africa’s Marco van Staden, before the yellow card was later upgraded by the Foul Player Review Officer. Van Staden also suffered the same fate after originally being sin-binned for retaliation.

The Foul Play Review Committee met in London on Tuesday and upheld the red card but deemed it worthy of low-entry level sanction. Sheehan will now miss the Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia at Allianz Stadium on Friday, as well as Leinster’s URC trip to Ospreys in the United Rugby Championship, on 4 December.

Rugby.title: Sheehan out of Wallabies Test after two-game ban

Rugby.copy:
Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two games after a croc-roll tackle against South Africa and will play no part against Australia on Friday night. The Leinster forward was shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley in the 72nd minute of Ireland's 20-17 victory over the Springboks in Dublin on Saturday.

That was later upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer (FPRO) on the basis of World Rugby's Law 9.20d that "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".

Rugby.title: Wallabies win over Wales far from perfect – but a lot better than recent weeks
Rugby.summary: Australia's display in Cardiff was not without fault, but it was a welcome boost at a time of year when other northern campaigns have come undone.
Rugby.copy:
There have been times in the last six or seven weeks where Australian rugby fans have wondered when – or if – the next Wallabies win might come. The Bledisloe Cup losses weren’t much fun, and there was a more than fair argument that the England and Scotland defeats, to start the November leg of the Nations Championship, were even worse. And knowing the Wallabies’ last two European tours both ended with a run of losses, it’s reasonable to assume that Australian confidence has taken a hit in recent times.

So it was pleasing to see the Wallabies start so well against Wales in Cardiff, adjust to the inevitable reactions, and complete the job at hand. Having spent the week celebrating maybe their greatest ever win, Wales were always going to be a tough prospect; the only unknowns were how much that masterful, but exhausting, win over New Zealand – and the aforementioned celebrations – had taken out of the Welsh players.

The 44-year-old refereed in his first Rugby World Cup in 2023 and has five Six Nations Championships behind him in the role, with this weekend’s clash the latest headline fixture in an officiating career that began 12 years ago.

Rugby.title: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts
Rugby.summary: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation: “We are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off.” And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep.

Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand.

Rugby.title: Unbeaten World Rugby Nations Cup winners name teams for final bout
Rugby.summary: The winners of Pools A and B in the World Rugby Nations Cup will meet in Tbilisi this weekend for bragging rights as the tournament's best.
Rugby.copy:
The winners of Pools A and B in the World Rugby Nations Cup will meet in Tbilisi this weekend for bragging rights as the tournament’s best. The USA enjoyed a blowout win over Romania in round 5 to secure their Pool A crown after four tight wins to begin the inaugural competition, while Georgia’s supremacy in Pool B has never been challenged, and they’ve emerged with a competition-best points differential of +124 through five rounds of action.

There is no further silverware on offer for the teams, but there’s an air of serendipity in the matchup coming in the final round of the competition. USA head coach Scott Lawrence has made just one change to the starting XV that put 53 points on Romania last weekend, with Mitch Wilson replacing Perry Mayo at fullback. And Georgia’s Pierre-Henry Broncan has also opted for as much continuity as possible, only promoting loosehead prop Sergo Abramishvili and halfback Gela Aprasidzeto to the starting team.

Last weekend’s starting XV wrote itself into Welsh rugby folklore by ending the 73-year wait for another win over the All Blacks. But that hasn’t stopped Tandy from making changes - with four new faces in his walk-on side for Saturday night.

It’s not a totally new combination - with Tandy reverting to the starting side that faced Japan at the start of the campaign. In the backs, Josh Adams is brought back into the left wing - having been rested last week - with Gabriel Hamer-Webb missing out.

Rugby.summary: PWR: RFU wants to 'protect Red Roses' with reduction in international players BBC
Rugby.copy:
World rugby has endured a few shocks and upsets in 2026 - and England's women losing back-to-back Test matches to Canada was among the biggest. But with 25 Canadians plying their trade on English soil in Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) last season, their success on the international stage comes at a time when PWR has been in discussions with the Rugby Football Union (RFU) to review the numbers of overseas players in the league.

"We are keen to attract star talent into PWR to continue to make it the best league in the world," said RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney. "But we've also got to protect England Red Roses' interests as well."

Rugby.title: Tamaiti Williams reaches major milestone in recovery from disc-eating infection
Rugby.summary: Tamaiti Williams has reached a significant milestone in his recovery from the back infection that ended his 2026 season after just two games for the Crusaders: running.
Rugby.copy:
Tamaiti Williams has reached a significant milestone in his recovery from the back infection that ended his 2026 season after just two games for the Crusaders: running. The All Blacks prop has been sidelined since discovering that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) had been eating a disc in his lower back, causing immense pain and putting more than just his rugby career in jeopardy.

Following a surgical procedure that included fusing two discs together, Williams has been slowly progressing through a lengthy rehab process as he eyes an eventual return to rugby.

Rugby.copy:
Rassie Erasmus has issued an invite to Springboks fans to join a watch party he is hosting online for South Africa’s Nations Championship test against Ireland. The coach is unable to attend the match due to a six-game ban he copped after a match-fixing rant following South Africa’s loss to France last week.

Under the rules of the ban, he will be unable to enter the stadium, communicate directly or indirectly with players or members of his staff during the match. The women's pool is China, Colombia, Mexico, Poland, Samoa and Uganda, with a first-time champion guaranteed after South Africa won last time. Dubai also hosts the opening SVNS Series stop, where New Zealand seek back-to-back titles.
Rugby.copy:
The Canadian Men’s Sevens side are heading back to Dubai this month, looking to defend their HSBC SVNS 3 crown against five challengers. But with only two sides able to progress to the second tier, there’s plenty at stake on November 27-28.

Canada wrapped up the inaugural SVNS 3 title by overcoming Belgium in January, while Samoa wrapped up third place. Samoa will look to go at least one better this time around, as teams look to take another step towards the SVNS World Championship.

Racket.summary: BWF World Tour Finals 2026: Full Qualifiers, Sindhu, Lakshya In Sportscape Magazine
bullets: The BWF has confirmed the top eight qualifiers in each of five events for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December, after the Hong Kong Open ended on 22 November. The prize pot is US$3.5 million, the biggest of the season.

India has two singles entries: world No.6 PV Sindhu, who qualified by winning the Hylo Open in Germany, and world No.11 Lakshya Sen, who got in after Koki Watanabe lost in the first round. World champion An Se Young is one title from a record 12 in a season.
Racket.copy:
The BWF World Tour Finals 2026 field is set for Hangzhou. See all qualifiers in five events, including India's PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen, and the USD 3.5 million prize pot. The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has released the list of the top eight qualifiers in the singles and doubles categories for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026. The list was confirmed after the Hong Kong Open ended on Sunday, 22 November. India has two entries in the World Finals qualifiers in the singles category, World No.6 PV Sindhu and World No.11 Lakshya Sen. Lakshya got in after Koki Watanabe lost in the first round, which also helped Chou Tien Chen and Kunlavut Vitidsarn. Sindhu qualified earlier after winning the Hylo Open 2026 in Germany.

An Se Young, the world champion, is one title away from a record of 12 titles in a season. Intanon earned a record 11th Finals qualification, and Sindhu is described as resurgent.

Racket.title: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
Racket.summary: French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.
Racket.copy:
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test. The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) confirmed the world number 57 is under investigation, after a report by L'Equipe, external earlier on Wednesday.

It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector". Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision.

Racket.title: Lehecka, Machac Lead Czechia Past Canada into Davis Cup Semifinals
Racket.summary: Lehecka, Machac Lead Czechia Past Canada into Davis Cup Semifinals Tennis Now
Racket.copy:
Czechia closed out Canada with conviction to return to its first Davis Cup semifinal in 12 years today. Jiri Lehecka defeated Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4), 6-2 clinching Czechia’s 2-0 Davis Cup quarterfinal triumph over Canada in Bologna, Italy.

It was Lehecka’s seventh win in his last eight Davis Cup singles matches and snapped Auger-Aliassime’s 10-match Davis Cup winning streak. Former US Open semifinalist Auger-Aliassime, who playing his first match since retiring from the Rolex Shanghai Masters round of 16 due to a knee injury last month, held a set point in the first set. Lehecka saved it aggressively attacking net to turn the set around.

Racket.title: Machac beats Draxl, Czechia leads Canada in Davis Cup Final 8 quarterfinal
Racket.summary: Machac beats Draxl, Czechia leads Canada in Davis Cup Final 8 quarterfinal Sportsnet.ca
Racket.copy:
Tomas Machac defeated Liam Draxl 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 Tuesday to give Czechia an early 1-0 lead over Canada in their Davis Cup Final 8 quarterfinal tie. Machac, ranked 59th in the world, won a clean first set in which he scored on both of his break points while defending the only one he faced.

Draxl, from Newmarket, Ont., rebounded in the second set. He overcame five aces and fought off four break points while scoring a key break to go up 4-2. Machac wrested the momentum back in the third set, clinching the match with his fourth break in the deciding game.

Racket.title: Renowned News Outlet Strikes $11 Million ATP Deal To Promote Tennis Across Its Home Nation
Racket.summary: Renowned News Outlet Strikes $11 Million ATP Deal To Promote Tennis Across Its Home Nation EssentiallySports
Racket.copy:
French tennis enthusiasts are set to be treated to a familiar name on their television screens. beIN Sports has won back the rights to the ATP Tour in France from 2028, and it hasn’t cost them an arm and a leg. According to L’Equipe, the Franco-Qatari channel will pay a little under 10 million euros, roughly 11 million dollars, a year across a four-year deal running to 2031, a deliberately restrained outlay for such a prized property.

The move, confirmed on 9 November, amounts to a homecoming of sorts. beIN Sports will broadcast the ATP in France before Eurosport got the rights, which means that the rights to the men’s tour are back on the channel. This time, however, it is coming back on its own terms – at a price that is more indicative of a leaner, more disciplined era in the business of broadcast rights than any of the crazy bidding that has occurred in the past few years.

Racket.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
Racket.summary: For big stars, endorsing companies like Kalshi and Polymarket is just another day in the beautiful business of being – and staying – rich When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Taking place inside the Supertennis Arena, Davis Cup Finals action will start on Tuesday, with eight nations all hoping they will lift the title come Sunday’s showpiece.

Each tie will consist of two singles rubbers followed by a deciding doubles rubber, if the tie is level at 1-1 following the opening singles matches. Racket.copy:
LONDON — U.S. Open champion Emma Raducanu joined Uniqlo’s charitable effort to support families facing hardship in the U.K. The Uniqlo global brand ambassador visited Little Village in Camden, where she met families, staff and volunteers, just as the retailer marked its donation of 16,800 Heattech items to 29 baby banks this year.

The visit, held around World Children’s Day on Nov. 20, was part of the retailer’s Heart of LifeWear initiative and its ongoing partnership with Save the Children. During her visit the brand said Raducanu spoke with a mother and her 4-year-old daughter about the support they had received from the baby bank. She also helped volunteers pack personalized bundles, which included Heattech clothing donated by Uniqlo alongside hygiene products, baby equipment, toys and books.

Alcaraz, still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following his injury scare earlier in the week, collapsed to the ground in celebration after sealing a 6-2 7-6 (9-7) win in a dramatic second-set tie-break.

Racket.title: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz beats world number one Alexander Zverev to claim title
Racket.summary: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz beats world number one Alexander Zverev to claim title BBC
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz outplayed world number one Alexander Zverev to end his wait for a first ATP Finals title and complete a remarkable post-injury return to the sport. A season which began with Alcaraz becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, before he was ruled out for more than four months with a wrist issue, ended with the Spaniard holding aloft another of the sport's biggest trophies.

Alcaraz, still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following his injury scare earlier in the week, collapsed to the ground in celebration after sealing a 6-2 7-6 (9-7) win in a dramatic second-set tie-break.

Racket.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev in ATP Finals title decider
Racket.summary: Carlos Alcaraz will face world number one Alexander Zverev for the ATP Finals title after completing a superb comeback victory against Ben Shelton.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz will face world number one Alexander Zverev for the ATP Finals title after completing a superb comeback victory against Ben Shelton. The indomitable Spaniard recovered from a flat start to outlast Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) and secure a return to the showpiece, 12 months after losing to Jannik Sinner.

Alcaraz again competed with strapping around his upper-left leg having injured his hamstring earlier this week, but produced his best tennis when it mattered most. The seven-time major winner, on a 13-match winning streak, will face Zverev in Sunday's final after the German beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7-0) 6-4.

Racket.copy:
Day 7 of the 2026 ATP Finals saw Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev book their places in Sunday’s championship match, setting up a fitting finale between the two standout players of the season.

Alcaraz had to work considerably harder than in his previous matches, recovering from a set down to defeat Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1). The American pushed him all the way, but a poor deciding tiebreak proved costly as the Spaniard extended his winning streak to 13 matches.

Racket.title: BREAKING NEWS: Zverev beats Medvedev to set up an ATP Finals final against Alcaraz
Racket.summary: BREAKING NEWS: Zverev beats Medvedev to set up an ATP Finals final against Alcaraz Tennis Majors
Racket.copy:
Alexander Zverev beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 in the second semi-final of the ATP Finals in Turin on Saturday. World No. 1 Alexander Zverev beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 in the second semi-final of the ATP Finals in Turin on Saturday to reach his third final at the event. On Sunday, the two-time champion will face Carlos Alcaraz, who beat Ben Shelton earlier in the day.

The serve dominated a first set made of short points: neither man faced a single break point in twelve games. Zverev then swept the tie-break 7-0. The first break point of the match only came after 71 minutes, on Medvedev’s serve at 3-3 in the second set, and Zverev converted his second opportunity to lead 4-3.

Golf.title: The longevity advantage: How PGA Tour, Cleveland Clinic are helping players stay competitive longer
Golf.summary: The longevity advantage: How PGA Tour, Cleveland Clinic are helping players stay competitive longer PGA Tour
Golf.copy:
The PGA Tour Performance Truck presented by Cleveland Clinic helps players stay healthy at every career stage. Editor’s note: This is Part 3 in a three-part series from the PGA Tour and Cleveland Clinic offering a behind-the-scenes look at today’s modern approach to player health and performance. This series explores what players can access inside the PGA Tour Performance Truck presented by Cleveland Clinic, how Cleveland Clinic experts use testing and insights to identify potential issues before they become injuries and how a comprehensive approach to health can help players stay competitive longer.

Longevity in professional golf isn't built overnight. For some players, it starts with the habits they establish as young professionals. For others, it means adapting to the physical demands of a career that can span decades. And increasingly, the conversation extends beyond how long a player can compete to how well he can live long after his playing days are over.

Golf.title: Brooks Koepka rule improves pro's PGA Tour status for 2027
Golf.summary: Brooks Koepka's return from LIV Golf benefitted many PGA Tour pros in 2026, including Max McGreevy on the last day of the season. The post Brooks Koepka rule improves pro’s PGA Tour status for 2027 appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Max McGreevy had just emptied the tank on the final day of the PGA Tour season. After a year in which he made 19 of 31 cuts but failed to produce any stellar results, the 31-year-old had needed to put together a good final round at the RSM Classic to give himself a chance at retaining some semblance of PGA Tour status.

But an even-par 70 at Sea Island left McGreevy tied for 10th. It was his best finish of the season but one that didn’t seem like it was going to be good enough to nudge him inside the top 125 to keep conditional status on the PGA Tour. When McGreevy walked off the course, he was bouncing between No. 126 and 127 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings. Those few spots are a huge difference — between getting 15-20 PGA Tour starts, as Lanto Griffin did in 2026 (17 starts) after finishing 125th last year, or largely plying your trade on the Korn Ferry Tour, as Frankie Capan III (only six PGA Tour starts), who finished 127th in 2025, did this year.

Golf.title: USGA, R&A provide significant update to golf equipment changes: Answering 5 burning questions
Golf.summary: The USGA and R&A have provided an update to plans to curb distance gains in pro golf that appear to show changes expected as soon as 2028. The post USGA, R&A provide significant update to golf equipment changes: Answering 5 burning questions appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The latest twist in the golf ball rollback saga has arrived. Late last week, the USGA and R&A quietly released a “notice to manufacturers” indicating they have identified two paths to limit distance gains in professional golf and are targeting approval of those changes in time for the start of the new PGA Tour schedule in 2028.

At first glance, the changes outlined by the governing bodies aim to limit distance gains for pro players with the driver and golf ball, but appear to fall short of the distance drops targeted by the golf ball rollback standard initially pursued back in 2023.

Golf.summary: David Puig’s Ryder Cup Dream Hits A New Road After LIV Collapse Yahoo Sports
Golf.copy:
David Puig has made his target crystal clear. The 24-year-old Spaniard wants a spot on Europe's 2027 Ryder Cup team. He told reporters that making the squad is "another dream of mine since I was young." This isn't just a side note for the young star. Puig sees the team at Adare Manor next September as his main goal now that the LIV Golf landscape has shifted.

Puig is starting his full season on the DP World Tour this week. He defends his Australian PGA Championship title in Sydney. The field includes major winners like Cameron Smith and Adam Scott. Puig knows the path is steep. In 2026, his world ranking peaked at 56th. A top-20 result was also achieved at the US PGA Championship. But the road to the Ryder Cup requires consistency. "Playing in a Ryder Cup would be amazing," Puig added, according to Golfmagic. "I'll try my best. Hopefully it's enough to be on the team in September."

Golf.title: Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young and Wyndham Clark headline PGA Tour Player of the Year award nominees
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young and Wyndham Clark headline PGA Tour Player of the Year award nominees CBS Sports
Golf.copy:
The PGA Tour on Tuesday announced nominees for the two major awards it hands out each year, Player of the Year and Rookie of the Year. Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick and Chris Gotterup make up the five-man race for the Jack Nicklaus Award, while Alex Fitzpatrick, Ben James, Kristoffer Reitan, Jackson Koivun and Marco Penge are among those vying for the Arnold Palmer Award.

Scheffler has become familiar with getting his hands on the Jack Nicklaus Award in recent years. The world No. 1 joined Tiger Woods as the only golfer to claim the title three years in a row when he secured the honor in 2024. After winning it again in 2025, Scheffler can join Woods again as the only players to ever win it five times in a row. The 15-time major champion won the award five straight seasons from 1999-2003 and three straight from 2005-07.

Golf.title: LIV Golf Creditors Threaten Chapter 7 Liquidation Over $2M Offer
Golf.summary: LIV Golf Creditors Threaten Chapter 7 Liquidation Over $2M Offer Front Office Sports
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy case in New Jersey is at risk of being converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation process. The official committee of unsecured creditors in LIV’s case does not support the current wind-down plan, which is offering just $2 million for general recovery claims. “At present, the plan only benefits the debtors’ current and former directors and officers and the Public Investment Fund of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia,” the committee wrote in a statement and reservation of rights filed Monday evening.

A Dec. 4 deadline has been set by the creditors and LIV to reach a deal or “immediately move to convert these cases to Chapter 7 and conduct an orderly liquidation of their assets.” In the meantime, settlement negotiations between all parties are underway. The creditors committee did not object to conditional approval of LIV’s revised disclosure statement and wind-down plan, which was granted by Judge Michael Kaplan on Tuesday morning.

Golf.title: Marco Penge claims maiden PGA Tour win: Englishman triumphs from four-way playoff at RSM Classic
Golf.summary: Marco Penge claims maiden PGA Tour win: Englishman triumphs from four-way playoff at RSM Classic Sky Sports
bullets: England's Marco Penge won his first PGA Tour title at the season-ending RSM Classic, emerging from a four-way playoff with Haotong Li, Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman, all on 16 under. He birdied the 18th again in the playoff after hitting his approach to 10 feet.

Penge, a three-time DP World Tour winner, needed a top-four finish to keep his PGA Tour card after a rookie season disrupted by viral illness. His final-round 65 earned the playoff place. The DP World Tour's BMW Australian PGA Championship begins on Thursday.
Golf.copy:
English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic. Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.

With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.

Golf.copy:
Jeeno Thitikul overcame both Nelly Korda and Annika Sorenstam Sunday at the CME Group Tour Championship. Thitikul beat Korda head-to-head in the LPGA’s season finale, earning another $4 million in official earnings. That jumped her past Sorenstam on the tour’s all-time money list.

Golf.summary: The Monday finish for the RSM Classic won't have fans. On Sunday, tournament host Davis Love III explained the controversial decision. The post The PGA Tour season will end without fans. Davis Love III defended the controversial decision appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
A lot will be on the line on Monday at Sea Island Resort when the 2026 PGA Tour season concludes. Players will be fighting to keep their PGA Tour cards, jump into the AON Next 10 or trying to secure the first win of their PGA Tour career.

But no one will be there to see the RSM Classic finish. After Saturday’s third round was washed out by rain, the tournament announced it would finish on Monday, but no fans would be allowed on the ground. Fans with Sunday tickets were allowed to watch the golf on Sunday, but Saturday tickets were not honored and fans were asked to see the refund policy since no crowds will be allowed on Monday.

Golf.summary: LPGA Tour: Jeeno Thitikul wins CME Group Tour Championship again and overtakes Annika Sorenstam's career money record Sky Sports
Golf.copy:
Jeeno Thitikul has won the LPGA Tour's season-ending CME Group Tour Championship for a third consecutive year after storming to a two-shot victory in Florida. Thitikul carded an eagle and five birdies during an impressive seven-under 65, pulling her clear of a congested leaderboard at Tiburon Golf Club and securing a 12th LPGA Tour title.

She finished on 24 under and two clear of Aki Iwai, who raced into contention with six birdies in the first 10 holes of her final-round 65, while world No 1 Nelly Korda finished in third spot.

Golf.copy:
World number two Jeeno Thitikul produced a seven-under final round of 65 to claim a third successive CME Group Tour Championship title. The 23-year-old from Thailand started the fourth round of the season-ending event with an eagle and went on to card five birdies as she finished on 24 under at the Tiburon Golf Club in Florida.

"The only words I have is not to change the course until I'm retired," said Thitikul. "It's just me and the course, we just are best friends. I think she is my best friend on the tour."

Golf.title: ‘It Threw Off Our Order’: Davis Love III Reveals How LIV Golf Pros Disrupted Team USA's Ryder Cup Order
Golf.summary: ‘It Threw Off Our Order’: Davis Love III Reveals How LIV Golf Pros Disrupted Team USA's Ryder Cup Order Yahoo Sports
Golf.copy:
A Ryder Cup captaincy is usually a queue. Names are pencilled in years ahead, future captains learn the job as assistants, and everyone knows who is next in line. Then LIV Golf walked in and started rubbing names off the list. That is how Davis Love III described the last few years on the Fully Equipped podcast. The former US captain explained how the Saudi-backed league unsettled Team USA's plans from the inside.

"But, you know, you've got to remember LIV Tour has had a huge impact. It wasn't a ripple effect. It was a bomb effect through all of golf. It threw off our order of captains. It left us not knowing if guys were going to be able to play or not. It obviously affected Europe more than us in terms of understanding who was going to get to play, but it threw us off our order. And then, obviously, Tiger threw us off the order a little bit as well," Love III said on the show.

Golf.title: Kim holds one-shot lead at LPGA finale as Korda closes in
Golf.summary: A-Lim Kim holds a slender lead going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship, with world number one Nelly Korda among the chasers.
Golf.copy:
South Korea's A-Lim Kim holds a slender lead going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship, with world number one Nelly Korda among the chasers. Kim, who held a three-shot overnight lead, carded a third round 69 which included six birdies and three bogeys, with two of those coming on the final three holes, to reach 18 under overall.

"I really focused on my game. Just aim and hit, that's all," said Kim. "Today the wind direction [was a] little tricky, changed a lot, swirly in the air. That's golf." In the chase for the $4m (£3.1m) top prize at the season-ending event, Japan's Yuri Yoshida and Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand are both on 17 under - one shot behind Kim.

Golf.title: PGA Tour season headed for Monday finish after rain washes out Saturday at RSM Classic
Golf.summary: Heavy rains washed out the third round of the RSM Classic on Saturday. The third round will be played on Sunday and the tournament will end on Monday. The post PGA Tour season headed for Monday finish after rain washes out Saturday at RSM Classic appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The 2026 PGA Tour season will last one day longer than expected. With pouring rain pummeling St. Simons Island, Georgia, the third round of the season-ending RSM Classic was postponed until Sunday. The final round will be played on Monday. It will be the PGA Tour’s third Monday finish of the fall slate.

“Obviously this is seaside golf, the golf course is very flat, the fairways are generally very flat with just a little bit of subtle movement,” PGA Tour chief referee Steve Rintoul told reporters on Saturday about the decision not to play on Saturday. “They’re above the marsh; they’re not sand-based. Even though it’s sea level, a dunes links look here, it’s not sand-based. So we had a lot of water sitting on the surface, especially in pockets in low areas in fairways where, I mentioned earlier, [we] may have a player who’s in the fairway in temporary water and needs to take relief, and that nearest point of relief takes him outside of the fairway. That takes the preferred lies out of his hands, and it just becomes, it’s not equitable when we get to that. So that kind of forced our hand.”

Because of “unplayable course conditions” at Sea Island's Seaside Course, no play was possible on Saturday, meaning the third round will now be played on Sunday, with the final round set for Monday.

A statement from the PGA Tour read: "Due to unplayable course conditions at Sea Island Golf Club resulting from inclement weather today, the third round of The RSM Classic will be contested on Sunday, November 22, with the final round to be played on Monday, November 23."

NAPLES, Fla. — Haeran Ryu of the Republic of Korea carded a bogey-free 6-under 66 on Thursday to sit T4 after the first round of the CME Group Tour Championship, one shot behind co-leaders Jeeno Thitikul, A Lim Kim and Karis Davidson at Tiburón Golf Club.

Golf.title: Thitikul, Kim and Davidson share CME Group Tour Championship lead
Golf.summary: Thitikul, Kim and Davidson share CME Group Tour Championship lead www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
The LPGA Tour's season finale has a crowded leaderboard after the first day. Jeeno Thitikul, A Lim Kim and Karis Davidson each opened the CME Group Tour Championship at Tiburón Golf Club with a 7-under-par 65. They share the lead at -7, one stroke ahead of a nine-player group at -6. With three rounds still to play, very little separates the top of the 60-player field.

Thitikul is the most closely watched of the three co-leaders. The world No. 2 won this event in 2024 and 2025 and arrived in Naples trying to win the Tour Championship for a third year in a row. Her bogey-free-looking start of seven under puts her right in contention, although that bid is still three rounds away from being decided. A Lim Kim of South Korea and Karis Davidson of Australia matched her score, so the opening round produced a three-nation tie between Thailand, Korea and Australia.

Golf.title: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play
Golf.summary: LPGA Tour introduce ‘aggressive’ new solution to stop slow play Yahoo
Golf.copy:
The LPGA Tour is tackling pace of play head-on. It's one of the biggest issues fans have with the modern game, as players are often taking around six hours to complete their rounds. And while the PGA Tour has often been criticized for not taking action to speed up the pace of play, the LPGA Tour is attempting to find solutions.

Their latest move is to fine any player who has been put on the clock over 35 times in a year $35,000. That's an extreme measure, considering the previous threshold was 40 holes, and the previous fine was $5,000.

Golf.title: Thitikul Stretches Tiburón Streak to Nine Straight Rounds in the 60s
Golf.summary: Thitikul Stretches Tiburón Streak to Nine Straight Rounds in the 60s www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
A Lim Kim has the lead at the CME Group Tour Championship. But the player behind her is the one who has owned Tiburón Golf Club for the past two years. Jeeno Thitikul has won this event in each of the last two years. On Friday in Naples, Florida, she shot 67 in the second round. That made it nine rounds in a row in the 60s for her at this course, and it keeps her in the race for a third straight title.

Thitikul is alone in second place at 12-under 132, three shots behind A Lim Kim. Kim leads at 15-under 129. Two rounds remain in the LPGA Tour's season finale, so the final weekend of the year now has a clear chase story.

Golf.summary: What to make of Tiger Woods' return to golf at Hero World Classic, Bryson DeChambeau's move to DP World Tour CBS Sports
Golf.copy:

Golf.title: DP World Tour 2027: Fewer cards, LIV ban and returning stars
Golf.summary: DP World Tour 2027: Fewer cards, LIV ban and returning stars www.golfpost.com
Golf.copy:
The DP World Tour has set its membership categories for the 2027 season, and the changes are significant. A total of 199 exempt members from 29 countries make up Categories 1 to 18. The number of full exempt cards falls from 110 to 100. Only the top 100 on the 2026 Race to Dubai Rankings keep full playing privileges, and players ranked 101 to 110 move into the conditional Category 18.

The pathways onto the tour are also narrower. At the Qualifying School Final Stage, the top 15 and ties now earn Category 18 membership, down from the top 20 and ties. Graduates from the HotelPlanner Tour, the tour's feeder circuit, fall from 20 to 15. Taken together, the changes are expected to leave about 20 fewer card holders in 2027.

Golf.title: UK firms owed thousands as Saudi-backed LIV paid golfers millions
Golf.summary: A BBC Sport investigation has found bills to UK companies were already overdue when LIV Golf made its final payments to players and executives before filing for bankruptcy.
bullets: BBC Sport has seen overdue invoices from five UK small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, unpaid by LIV Golf before it filed for bankruptcy. They include £321,671 owed to caterer Global Infusion Group and £75,225 owed to cleaning firm BD365 Clean.

Court filings show LIV paid golfers $16.6m on 31 July and $34.2m between 17 August and 3 September, including $6.4m to Jon Rahm. Only $2m has been earmarked for unsecured creditors, while LIV estimates liabilities of $500m to $1bn and at least 1,000 creditors.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf - backed by more than $5bn (£3.8bn) from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund - paid millions to players and executives in the weeks before filing for bankruptcy, while leaving a trail of unpaid bills from UK suppliers.

BBC Sport has seen invoices from five small businesses totalling hundreds of thousands of pounds, all of which were overdue before LIV made its final payments to players. Global Infusion Group,, external a Buckinghamshire company that provided catering at July's LIV Golf UK event, is still owed £321,671, due on 7 August.
